subject: Prod quota design & target unit-econ for BlueHarbor pilot

Subject: Prod quota design & target unit-econ for BlueHarbor pilot

Hi Sara — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps from today’s discovery so the team is aligned:

Call recap (high level)
- Primary use: customer-facing conversational assistant for order tracking and SSO-enabled support flows.
- Typical steady-state: ~600k tokens/day (mostly short prompts + short responses).
- Campaign/peak pattern: spikes to ~6–8M tokens/day for 30–90 minute windows during scheduled marketing pushes.
- Latency target: p95 < 400ms for user-facing completions.

Key commercial items we discussed
1) Target unit economics: you mentioned a preferred target in the ~$900–1,200 per 1M token range. Please confirm if $/1M target is flexible.
2) Budget range: high-level FY27 pilot budget band (for evaluation) — you suggested $20k–$60k. Confirm if that’s for the whole pilot period or monthly.
3) Rate limits & burst behavior: you need baseline rate limit for daytime traffic and a short-duration burst allowance for campaigns. We need expected QPS and burst duration to size the pilot.

Proposed next steps (our side)
- Jordan: send a concise cost model showing $/1M tokens at a few quantization/throughput configs + sample billing scenarios for your projected volumes. (attached: pilot-proposal-blueharbor_v1.pdf)
- Neha: prepare a recommended quota proposal (baseline quota, burst pool, overage tiers) and a pilot SOW template.
- Marissa: start procurement checklist (PO/contracting path) and propose calendar slots for kickoff.

Questions for you
- Can you confirm expected sustained QPS during normal operations and expected peak QPS during campaign spikes?
- Is the $20k–$60k band monthly or total pilot spend?
- Any procurement/contracting constraints (PO required, contract signer)?

Thanks — aiming to send the cost model + quota proposal tomorrow morning PST.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Prod quota design & target unit-econ for BlueHarbor pilot

Jordan, thanks for the recap — helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

Numbers and budget
- Steady-state: yes ~600k tokens/day.
- Peaks: during promos we hit ~7–8M tokens over ~45–60 mins; occasional bigger spikes (very rare) up to ~12M for ~10–20 mins.
- QPS: steady ~40–70 QPS, peaks up to ~220–250 QPS for short windows.
- Budget: the $20k–$60k band is for the initial 6–8 week pilot total, not monthly. We are trying to keep pilot spend under $50k if possible.
- Target unit-econ: internal goal is ~$1,000 per 1M tokens, but we can stretch to ~$1,200 depending on SLA/ingress guarantees.

Procurement
- We will require a standard PO and vendor onboarding; legal will ask for basic SOC2 language.

Asks from you
- Please provide a sample cost calc that hits ~$1k and $1.2k per 1M token scenarios and show what tradeoffs (quantization, batching, reserved vs on-demand) make that possible.
- Recommend a quota design that avoids throttling legit campaign spikes but controls runaway cost — what baseline + burst pool would you propose?

I'll get you the formal PO path and the procurement lead's contact later today.

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Product Ops | BlueHarbor Logistics
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod quota design & target unit-econ for BlueHarbor pilot

Hi Sara — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. Attached are two artifacts: a concise cost model (redwood-unit-econ-1M.csv) and a recommended quota sketch. Summary of options below.

Unit-econ scenarios (all numbers $ per 1M tokens, illustrative)
- On-demand (no reserved): $1,450 / 1M tokens — highest flexibility, lowest commitment.
- Reserved small pilot (commit 50M tokens total over pilot): $1,100 / 1M tokens — assumes mixed batching, standard FP16 on our mid-tier GPU.
- Reserved + quantized path (commit 75M + use int8-quantized runtime for chat model): $950 / 1M tokens — best for hitting your ~$1k target (tradeoff: slightly higher latency in tail under heavy KV-loads).

Recommended quota design (pilot)
- Baseline daily quota: 5M tokens/day (covers normal + headroom).
- Burst pool: 25M tokens available per week that can be consumed in bursts; this is a soft pool that we allocate to avoid immediate throttling.
- Short-duration QPS allowance: baseline rate-limit 120 QPS, automatically scales via burst token consumption up to 260 QPS for windows up to 30 minutes; sustained higher QPS will draw from the weekly burst pool.
- Overage pricing: if burst pool is exhausted, overage billed at 1.5x reserved rate for the pilot period; for pilots on the quantized reserved plan the overage multiplier is 1.3x.

Examples (simplified)
- If you use 600k/day steady + one 60-minute 8M spike in a week and are on the 75M reserved+quant path, expected pilot spend ~ $38k (est). Full calc in attached CSV.

Next steps
- Neha: can you convert this sketch into a short SOW + formal quota table we can attach to the pilot PO?
- Marissa: can you confirm procurement timeline and whether we need any special contracting language for SOC2 phrasing?

I’ll also flag this for our pricing team if BlueHarbor wants an expanded reserved commitment — they may be able to improve the 1M token price further with a 6–12 month commit.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
